verdict_text: YES. The script slices the head-bearing tensors correctly: for each of the 16 layers, the keep index for a single 2048-wide segment with 128-wide blocks and `DROP_HEAD = 5` yields indices 0..639 followed by 768..2047 in order, applied on rows (dim 0) for q, k, v and on columns (dim 1) for o_proj, giving `[1920, 2048]` and `[2048, 1920]` with dtype preserved. All other tensors and names are left untouched, the five required checks are asserted before the write, and the result is saved as a single `out/T2/model.safetensors` with 114 tensors. The only assumption is that the external `_ckpt.load_checkpoint` helper loads the sharded input into a plain name-to-tensor dict, which is what the script relies on.
